goal.source_text: More downforce without going over 15 N of drag at 25 m/s. You can change the angle, span, flap and endplates. Keep the chord.
assumptions: Chord, airfoil, mounts and ride height stay fixed.

design_space.name: FSAE-style rear wing

parameters.name: chord_mm
parameters.description: Total chord, main element plus flap

parameters.name: flap_chord_frac
parameters.description: Flap chord as a fraction of total chord

notes: Ranges from PLAN.md B.5; W-B owns the real solver and may narrow them before CP-B.

metric_catalog.name: downforce_n
metric_catalog.description: Downforce at the design speed (VLM + viscous correction + endplates)

metric_catalog.name: drag_n
metric_catalog.description: Total drag: induced + section profile + endplate friction

metric_catalog.name: drag_profile_n
metric_catalog.description: Section profile drag (NeuralFoil) plus endplate skin friction

metric_catalog.name: cl
metric_catalog.description: Wing lift coefficient on planform area

metric_catalog.name: stall_margin_deg
metric_catalog.description: Section stall angle minus angle of attack (negative = stalled)

metric_catalog.name: span_efficiency
metric_catalog.description: Oswald e from Prandtl lifting-line theory for the planform

payload.rationale: Drag is 11.3 N against the 15 N limit and stall margin is 3.5 deg against 2.0 deg. Raising angle of attack raises downforce roughly linearly, costs drag and stall margin. Bracketing 7 and 8 deg tests how much headroom there is.

payload.explanation: Raising AoA from 6 to 7 deg gave only +1.44% downforce (CL 1.152 to 1.168), far below my 6-25% prediction, though direction was up. Drag rose 4.22%, mostly profile drag (+9.13%) versus induced (+2.91%). Stall margin fell 3.5 to 2.5 deg, as predicted. Design stays feasible, so accepted.
payload.lesson: Near stall, extra AoA yields little lift but costs profile drag and stall margin, so the lift slope is shallow here.

payload.rationale: Stall margin is binding at 2.5 deg, so AoA and flap are risky. Induced drag is 9.18 N of 11.8 N drag; more span and taller endplates raise aspect ratio, adding downforce within the drag limit without changing section angles.

payload.explanation: Accepted: downforce rose 21.6% (above my 5-18% range) and aspect ratio rose 19.9%, as predicted. But drag rose 9.99% and induced drag rose 5.33%, not down. Larger area and lift (CL up 3.36%) outweighed the AR benefit; profile drag jumped 26.5%. Stall margin stayed 2.5.
payload.lesson: Extra span adds wing area and lift, so induced drag can rise despite higher aspect ratio; profile drag grows with area.

payload.explanation: Increasing flap chord fraction from 0.3 to 0.35 raised downforce 2.48% and drag 6.55%, matching all four predictions. Profile drag rose 11.1% versus induced 5.02%, so the larger flap costs mostly viscous drag. Stall margin stayed 2.5 deg, so L/D fell 3.82%.
payload.lesson: Lengthening the flap chord adds downforce cheaply on stall margin, but profile drag grows faster than lift, lowering L/D.

payload.explanation: Raising endplates from 250 to 300 mm lifted effective aspect ratio 6.44%, cutting induced drag 5.57% and total drag 2.26%, as predicted. Downforce rose only 0.258%, below the 0.5% floor, so that call missed. Profile drag rose 6.99%, likely from more endplate wetted area. Stall margin stayed 2.5 deg.
payload.lesson: Taller endplates reliably cut induced drag via aspect ratio, but add profile drag and give only negligible downforce gain.

payload.explanation: Raising flap angle from 15 to 18 deg did not add downforce (-0.1%, CL 1.24 vs 1.24); I predicted +1 to 8%. Profile drag rose 36.2% (3.89 to 5.29 N) while induced drag was flat, so drag hit 10.3% and L/D fell 9.42%. Stall margin dropped to 2.0 deg, so the flap likely separated.
payload.lesson: Past about 15 deg this flap likely separates, so more angle adds profile drag and stall-margin loss without downforce.
